## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Fix the `isAccessTokenId` matcher, which never checks the grant shortcut

Affected:
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:476-492

Explanation:
The matcher has two bugs:

- **Wrong offset.** The decoder reads the grant shortcut with `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`. The matcher instead uses `substring(3, 5)`, so for `"onrtac"` it reads `"ta"`.
- **Inverted condition.** It returns `false` when the substring *equals* the expected shortcut.

Because of the wrong offset, the comparison is effectively never true. Every well-formed `xxxxxx:UUID` therefore passes. The updated assertions (code-to-token, device, refresh, CIBA) give false confidence that the correct grant type is encoded.

The matcher also has no length check. A prefix shorter than 5 characters throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning a failed match.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
String[] items = item.split(":");
if (items.length != 2 || items[0].length() != 6) return false;
if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
return isUUID().matches(items[1]);
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Make the new `getShortcut()` SPI method safe and validate shortcuts at startup

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29-33
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-85

Explanation:
`getShortcut()` is a new abstract method with no default. This breaks custom grant types and can stop the server from starting:

- **Old compiled extensions.** A custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` built against the previous SPI throws `AbstractMethodError` when `postInit` calls `gtf.getShortcut()`.
- **Null shortcuts.** An implementation that returns `null` makes `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throw an NPE.
- Both failures happen in `postInit`, so a single third-party grant prevents startup.

Shortcut format is not validated either:

- The javadoc says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters". The decoder, however, rejects any prefix that is not exactly 6 characters (2+2+2).
- A 3-character shortcut, or one containing `:`, produces token IDs that `encodeTokenId` accepts but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects.
- The duplicate check only compares the sizes of the two maps. It does not reject collisions with the reserved `na` shortcut.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc: "must be exactly 2 characters, unique across grants"
// optionally: default String getShortcut() { return null; }

// postInit:
String sc = gtf.getShortcut();
if (sc == null || sc.length() != 2 || sc.indexOf(':') >= 0 || DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN.equals(sc)) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Grant '" + gtf.getId() + "' must define a unique 2-char shortcut, got: " + sc);
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Derive the lightweight-token flag from the token's client, not the session-context client

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:54-55
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1052-1054

Explanation:
`initToken` now calls `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` for every access token. That method dereferences `session.getContext().getClient()`. Previously it ran only inside protocol mappers.

On token-creation paths where the context client is unset, or differs from the client the token is issued for (e.g. admin "generate example token"), this has two possible outcomes:

- an NPE, which breaks token issuance, or
- the wrong `lt`/`rt` flag encoded into the `jti`.

Use the client from the client session instead.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
ClientModel client = clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient();
Object attr = session.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED);
boolean useLightweightToken = Boolean.parseBoolean(client.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED))
        || Boolean.TRUE.equals(attr);
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Performance
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Remove per-request provider rescans and unchecked map overwrites in grant lookups

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:106-137

Explanation:
`getGrantTypeByShortcut` is reached from `getTokenContextFromTokenId`, which parses token IDs that may be client-supplied. Each unknown shortcut streams over all `OAuth2GrantType` factories, and misses are never cached. Random 2-character grant segments therefore force a full scan on every request.

Both refresh paths also insert mappings without the duplicate validation that `postInit` performs. A late-deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites `grantsByShortcuts`. Tokens from one grant would then decode as another, which breaks the bidirectional invariant.

Rely on the maps built in `postInit`. If hot deployment must be supported, rebuild and validate the maps on provider (re)deploy events rather than on the request path.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
protected String getGrantTypeByShortcut(String shortcut) {
    return grantsByShortcuts.get(shortcut); // rebuilt on provider deploy events, with duplicate check
}
protected String getShortcutByGrantType(String grantType) {
    return grantsToShortcuts.get(grantType);
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Null-check `rawTokenId` instead of checking `grantType` twice

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:72-73

Explanation:
Line 73 is a copy-paste error: it calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`. As a result, `rawTokenId` is never checked. A null `rawTokenId` is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` then emits a malformed ID ending in `:null`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Consensus: 2/3 reviewers
Title: Keep the cached `grantType` in sync with form params and restore the removed copy constructor

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:99-103

Explanation:
Two related problems in `Context`:

- **Stale `grantType`.** The value is captured once in the constructor. `setFormParams` can later replace `formParams` without updating it, so the two can drift apart.
- **Removed copy constructor.** The public `Context(Context)` constructor was deleted. Extensions that copy a grant context will fail to compile, or fail at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
public Context(Context context) {
    // ... existing copies ...
    this.grantType = context.grantType;
}

public void setFormParams(MultivaluedHashMap<String, String> formParams) {
    this.formParams = formParams;
    this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);
}
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Assert the specific failure in `testIncorrectGrantType`, which currently passes via an NPE

Affected:
- services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:77-85

Explanation:
In this test the factory's `sessionFactory` is null. When the lookup of `"ac"` misses, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` enters the refresh branch and throws an NPE. The broad `catch (RuntimeException)` swallows it.

The intended "Unknown value ... for grant type" `IllegalArgumentException` path is therefore never exercised, and regressions in that path would be hidden.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// Provide a mock sessionFactory (or guard null in the refresh path), then:
} catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
    Assert.assertTrue(expected.getMessage().contains("for grant type"));
}
~~~

## 8) Severity: LOW | Type: Security
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Avoid echoing raw, untrusted token IDs in exception messages

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-94

Explanation:
`getTokenContextFromTokenId` parses the `jti` of presented tokens, which may be attacker-controlled. The exception messages concatenate the full, unbounded `encodedTokenId`. If these exceptions are logged or returned, this enables log injection (CR/LF) and log flooding. Include only short, sanitized fragments, or none.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
throw new IllegalArgumentException("Incorrect token id format. Expected 6-char context prefix.");
// ...
throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown session type shortcut in token id");
~~~
